Over 80 double tax conventions (DTCs), including with France, Germany, Netherlands, UK, USA, China, UAE, Singapore

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or authorized signatories under private deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice for foreign-issued ancillary documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration / Certificate of Good Standing for each non-resident corporate partner or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all direct and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport issuing authority of each individual's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form identifying individuals owning or controlling more than 25% of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg law firm or notary supervising the incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and registration with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the client and/or corporate partners for AML/KYC verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if certified by a foreign notary; otherwise original bank attestation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons (PEPs) and family members/close associates; required screening against EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (CFSD), OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, Luxembourg financial sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Finance, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists; ongoing transaction monitoring and risk-based refresh screening for the life of the entity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any language using Latin (Roman) script; if the proposed name uses non-Latin alphabets, a mandatory Latin-script transliteration must be registered. Filings with the RCS are made in French or German. The name must end with the legal form indicator 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale' and must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or infringe prior rights.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg - if it implies state affiliation or government sponsorship
Fonds / Fund / SICAV / SIF (regulated fund terminology)
Chamber of Commerce / Chambre de Commerce
European / EU / Union Européenne (if misrepresenting official EU connection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a refusal by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant may file a revised name application. To contest a definitive refusal, a written administrative réclamation must be lodged with the LBR within one month of notification; if rejected, an appeal may be brought before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of the adverse decision. Legal representation by a Luxembourg counsel is required for contested appeals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally accepted for RCS registration provided a Luxembourg address accepts service of process. However, for this industry (offshore towage and salvage) with SCSp structure, a virtual address alone is insufficient for economic substance; the entity must maintain a physical operational presence, administrative office, local management, and accounting substance in Luxembourg to satisfy commercial substance expectations and tax transparency requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk; unannounced physical on-site inspections by Luxembourg tax and CSSF authorities are estimated at a 25% annual probability for an active commercial SCSp engaged in cross-border towage/salvage activities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), including the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) regime introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers; Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Duly executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) or notarial deed deposited with the LBR for inscription in the RCS and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital and no escrow or blocked-account requirement under Luxembourg law for an SCSp. Contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement; cash contributions may be called or deposited according to contract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT WAS RESOLVED at the first meeting of the general partner of the SCSp that: (1) the initial capital interests set out in Schedule A are subscribed and credited to the partners' capital accounts; (2) the registered office is established at [registered address], Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed sole general manager and [Name] is appointed compliance officer, each with power to open bank accounts, sign contracts, and issue Lloyds_Standard_Form_Wire payment instructions; (4) the partnership agreement, as executed, is ratified; and (5) the managers are authorized to complete RCS registration, RESA publication, and all tax and maritime licence filings. This resolution is valid from the date passed and until revoked in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS Name Desk, via guichet.lu online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names online and pay the applicable search or reservation fee. The chosen name must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must clearly identify the undertaking. A positive name reservation letter is issued upon acceptance.
required_dossiers: Proof of power of representation if filed by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused or flagged, the RCS issues a reasoned refusal; replace with an alternate proposed name and resubmit within the observation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of registered office and domiciliation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent approved by the CSSF, or a landlord in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a standard domiciliation agreement providing a registered office address in Luxembourg and use of mailing and convening facilities. The domiciliation agent handles official correspondence and maintains records required under AML and KYC rules.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of the general partner or manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the domiciliation provider rejects the KYC file, remediate documentary deficiencies first; if still refused, select an alternative licensed domiciliation agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary when the partnership agreement is made notarial or when contributions in rem are made; otherwise the partners themselves by private signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the statutory clauses: legal form (SCSp), firm name, registered office, corporate object comprising deep-sea tugboat towage and maritime emergency salvage, duration, profit and loss sharing, identity and powers of the general partner, capital interests and subscription of the limited partners, management provisions, and indemnities. Execute the deed in original or notarial form.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of all partners and managers
Proof of lawful source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial execution reveals inconsistencies, execute a rectification addendum prior to deposit; clerical errors can be corrected by additional notarial act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the LBR online filing portal and submit the executed partnership agreement, domiciliation attestation, proof of appointment of the general partner, and sworn legalization certificates. Upon validation, the RCS assigns a registration number and the legal notice is published in RESA.
required_dossiers: Original or certified copy of the executed partnership agreement or notarial deed
Identity documents of the general partner or partners
Criminal record extract of managers not older than three months
Declaration of no prior bankruptcy or disqualification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an observation, correct and resubmit the electronic file within the assigned legal deadline; if the filing is suspended, apply for an extension through LBR customer service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for tax, VAT, social security and maritime operator formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD), Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines / VAT (AEDT), Common Centre for Social Security (CCSS), and the Maritime Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration extract to the tax authorities to obtain an LU tax number and VAT number; register as an employer with CCSS; file seafarer and Maritime Labour Convention declarations; apply for the maritime transport and assistance licence with the Maritime Administration, attaching proof of insurance for towage and salvage operations.
required_dossiers: Insurance cover notes, including P&I and H&M
Form 500 and relevant amended registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authorities request further information, provide the missing documents within the stipulated timeframe; preliminary positions may be obtained by filing a binding tax ruling request with ACD.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration de la navigation maritime, Maritime Administration, Ministry of Mobility and Public Works, Luxembourg
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Maritime Assistance and Towing Service Operating Licence (Autorisation d'exploitation de services d'assistance et de remorquage en mer)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Luxembourg Environment Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Environmental Notice by exemption; no full EIA is mandatory for offshore towage and salvage contracts unless a shore base is operated in Luxembourg, in which case a Category B screening under the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL 73/78 Annexes I to VI, EU Directive 2005/35/EC on ship-source pollution, Directive (EU) 2016/802 on sulphur content of marine fuels, and Luxembourg waste handling regulations; oily-water separation must limit discharge to below 15 parts per million; zero-discharge standards apply in special areas; all salvage waste must be delivered to approved port reception facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspection for any Luxembourg shore office, repair quay, or storage facility issued by the communal fire brigade and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines; workplace authorization and occupational health certificates for seafarers required under the Maritime Labour Convention 2006 and SOLAS.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD / Luxembourg Inland Revenue) — portal: eSpace (espace.impotsdirects.public.lu) and MyGuichet.lu (www.myguichet.lu). Indirect taxes (VAT, registration duties, stamp duties): Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — registration and returns via MyGuichet.lu. Customs: Administration des Douanes et Accises (IDA) via the Luxembourg Single Window for export clearance. All national registrations are coordinated with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — RCS: The SCSp must be registered with the RCS through MyGuichet.lu (Form A, creation of a special limited partnership) despite lacking separate legal personality; the RCS issues the business registration number (matricule). Step 2 — Direct tax: upon RCS registration, the ACD automatically allocates the 11-digit Luxembourg national identification/tax number (numéro d'identification); a non-resident enterprise without an RCS presence files the direct-tax registration form with the ACD via MyGuichet.lu eDesk. Step 3 — VAT: file Form 640 'Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA' with the AEDT (online via MyGuichet.lu), obtaining a Luxembourg VAT number in format LU + 8 digits; a fiscal representative established in Luxembourg is required for non-EU persons without an establishment. Step 4 — Complete any social/statistical declarations through the Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS) as a complement to fiscal registration. Fully digitized filings via MyGuichet.lu are activated within approximately 10 business days for manual review cases.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — By default, the SCSp is fiscally transparent: it is not subject to corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT) or net wealth tax (NWT) at entity level; each partner is assessed directly on his distributive share of income. Foreign partners are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg real estate, consistent with Territorial_Scope. No Tax_Exempt_Zone applies. The SCSp is not itself the VAT taxable person for its supplies; the gérant/managing partner or a designated representative supplies the towage/salvage services in a representative capacity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. However, under Article 2 of the Law of 18 December 2015 (amending the Tax Adaptation Law, Steueranpassungsgesetz) and ACD Circular L.G. - A n° 72 of 26 January 2016, an SCSp may elect opaque status (fully subject to CIT/MBT/NWT) by including an express clause in the partnership agreement or by filing a declaration with the ACD; the election is binding for at least five consecutive fiscal years. For hybrid mismatch mitigation (ATAD implementation, Law of 21 December 2018), partners may apply domestic alignment tie-breaker elections to prevent double non-taxation where Luxembourg transparency conflicts with the partner's jurisdiction classification; such elections are permitted only within the limits of EU anti-hybrid rules and the applicable double tax treaty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small-business exemption under Article 57 Loi TVA; raised from EUR 30,000 effective 1 January 2023). This threshold applies to Luxembourg-established taxable persons; non-established foreign suppliers engaged in Luxembourg taxable activities must register without regard to the threshold except where the reverse-charge or OSS/IOSS regimes apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, API validation gateway or digital stamping applies to standard B2B supplies. Luxembourg has adopted a phased B2B e-invoicing mandate (Budget Law 2024, adopted December 2023): from 1 January 2026, every VAT-registered business must be able to receive structured electronic invoices; from 1 January 2027, mandatory issuance applies to businesses with an annual turnover exceeding EUR 100,000, using the PEPPOL network (structured formats such as UBL and Factur-X). B2G e-invoicing has been obligatory via PEPPOL since 2020 (transposition of Directive 2014/55/EU). VAT records and e-invoices must be archived in their original structured electronic form for at least 10 years; the AEDT does not operate an electronic clearance/validation gateway and no fiscal stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: exports to non-EU third countries are zero-rated under Article 49 Loi TVA if physical transport outside the EU is proven (electronic customs export declaration accepted; exit evidence within 3 months). Services: (i) B2B supplies to a non-Luxembourg business customer are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (place of supply = customer's establishment, Article 58 Loi TVA), effectively 0% with reverse charge in the customer's country; (ii) services to meet the direct needs of sea-going vessels used in international navigation, including tugboat towage and maritime salvage of such vessels and their cargo, are exempt with credit (zero-rated) under Article 51 Loi TVA, transposing Article 148(d) of the VAT Directive; (iii) salvage/towage performed on the high seas outside Luxembourg territorial waters generally falls under the B2B place-of-supply rule (customer location) or qualifies as a zero-rated ancillary service to international transport. To claim 0%, the taxpayer must evidence the customer's non-resident/VAT status, a written standard-form contract of towage/salvage (e.g., Lloyd's Open Form, BIMCO TOWCON/TOWLINE), the commercial invoice, payment proof and, where goods are involved, the customs export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / electronic export entry filed with the Luxembourg IDA or the customs office of EU exit) evidencing EU departure and the exit date for zero-rating of goods
Bill of Lading (or Sea Waybill) for the towage/salvage voyage, showing vessel, route and cargo as proof of international transport/salvage and the export movement

Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or foreign-exchange confirmation) evidencing receipt of the contractual consideration in foreign currency within the commercial credit period (standard commercial benchmark: 180 days; not a Luxembourg statutory deadline)

Original or certified copy of the towage/salvage contract (Lloyd's Standard Form of Salvage Agreement or Offshore Towing Agreement) specifying parties, services, day rates/lump sum, and place of performance
Commercial invoice marked zero-rated (0% TVA) referencing the applicable Luxembourg VAT article and identifying the non-EU customer, vessel IMO number and voyage
Supporting transport evidence: vessel Lloyds/IMO registration, port-call certificates, master's signed towage/salvage confirmation, or assistance/fixture notes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg does not impose a statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export zero-rating claims; documentation of payment/repatriation within a commercial period (commonly 180 days) is nevertheless an audit expectation, and proceeds that remain offshore or uncollected may trigger transfer-pricing adjustment, deemed distributions to partners, or CFC/reporting consequences. Where the AEDT establishes that zero-rating is unjustified or fraudulent (forged export declarations or Bills of Lading, circular towage invoicing, false high-seas salvage claims, missing exit proof), the authorities claw back the unpaid VAT at the standard rate (17%) plus statutory late-payment interest (0.6% per month), impose administrative penalties of up to 100% of the tax evaded in cases of bad faith, and may pursue criminal sanctions: imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fines up to EUR 250,000 for natural persons, and fines up to EUR 500,000 for legal entities, under Article 53 of the Loi TVA and the amended General Tax Law (2022 reform). The gérant/managing partner and partners may be held jointly and severally liable. In fraud cases, the limitation period extends to 10 years, permitting retrospective reopening of assessments, suspension of the VAT number, and publication of sanctions on the tax-fraud register.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); prudential supervision and financial-market conduct oversight shared with Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); Ministry of Finance responsible for legislative framework
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-zone member with full capital and current-account convertibility under TFEU Articles 63-65. There are no exchange controls, prior authorisation requirements, or restrictions on repatriation of profits for SCSp partners whether resident or non-resident. Inward and outward payments are subject exclusively to EU sanctions regulations, EU AML/CTF rules, and CSSF/BCL reporting thresholds. Partner profit distributions from an SCSp are generally taxable at the level of each partner and, for Luxembourg-resident taxable partners, subject to standard corporate/personal income rules; no special remittance tax or conversion requirement applies. For non-resident partners, no Luxembourg withholding on liquidation proceeds is imposed if the SCSp is treated as fiscally transparent under Luxembourg law, but distributions in liquidation/redemption may be classified as income if anti-abuse rules and substance indicators are not met.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Luxembourg. Export proceeds may be retained in any currency and in any EEA bank account or Luxembourg foreign-currency account. Under EU Regulation No 184/2016 (balance-of-payments statistics) and BCL rules, resident entities must report annual transactions with non-resident counterparties exceeding EUR 250,000 for services, financing, and investment flows; foreign-currency balances are reported quarterly for monetary financial institution statistics. Invoices and receipts from offshore towage and salvage services to non-EU clients should be coded under the appropriate balance-of-payments classification (services) and relevant purpose code; no surrender or conversion is mandated.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI viability is Low to Medium. Only EEA-licensed electronic-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions authorized under PSD2 and supervised in Luxembourg or passported from another EEA state may lawfully execute payments into or out of Luxembourg. Fully offshore, non-EEA digital EMIs (e.g., operating under unregulated or partial crypto/digital licences) cannot provide clearing or settlement services for a Luxembourg SCSp without a Luxembourg banking or EMI licence. A CSSF-authorised EMI or a passported EEA EMI may be used for operational liquidity and small-value towage-mobilisation payments, but it is not a substitute for a tier-1 bank for capital injections, escrowed salvage awards, or high-value Lloyds Standard Form disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a statutory obligation for all directors/partners to appear physically at a bank branch if a compliant video-identification and remote onboarding procedure is used by the bank. In practice, tier-1 banks require a face-to-face or equivalent double-video-call interview for legal-entity customers whose beneficial owners or general partners are non-resident and for high-risk maritime counterparties. For an SCSp, at least one general partner or a duly authorised signatory with power of representation should undergo physical identification in Luxembourg or at a European Union bank branch; the general partner's corporate documents, a notarised extract of the SCSp partnership agreement, and the ultimate beneficial owner declaration must be apostilled and, if necessary, translated into English, German, or French depending on the bank's KYC policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of SCSp beneficial ownership and changeable limited-partner registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current full-chain ownership breakdown through to natural persons; signed ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declarations per CSSF Regulation 12/02; excerpts of the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register or, if unregistered, a sworn declaration by the general partner; partnership agreement with contribution schedules; bank-issued reference or legal-opinion wrapper confirming fiscal transparency and non-recourse nature of limited partner interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Maritime sanction exposure, vessel flag, or salvage-counterparty connection to sanctioned states/entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lloyd's Register/EQUASIS or other IMO vessel certificate; flag-state registry excerpt; International Group P&I Club certificate of entry; sanctions targeted-screening reports on all vessel owners, charterers, towage counterparties, and salvage creditors; ship position list and AIS history; contract-specific OFAC/EU assessment by a reputable maritime sanctions counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual inbound capital injection from non-EU related party or escrow agent in excess of bank expectations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed equity/partnership-capital commitment agreement; underlying towage or salvage master agreement referencing stage payments and escrow release conditions; invoice or progress certificate; SWIFT instruction with exact purpose code and beneficiary account nomenclature; board or general-partner resolution approving the transaction and identity of counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions into the Luxembourg SCSp must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the remitter's tier-1 bank to the SCSp's Luxembourg euro or USD account. Luxembourg banks apply BCL balance-of-payments reporting and require the purpose code to reflect inward direct investment in partnership capital (e.g., 'CAPCONT' or EU BoP code for direct investment equity). Beneficiary reference must include the SCSp name and project ID. For salvage/towage contracts structured as escrow releases, the escrow bank must transmit funds with the escrow release instruction and a copy of the legally binding salvage agreement or Lloyds Open Form; the receiving bank will verify that the remitter is not a blocked entity and that beneficial ownership aligns with the RBE filing. Payment details should be pre-agreed via a sworn account-signing mandate and the bank's 'customer information sheet' to prevent delays.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for towage and salvage operations—fuel purchases, dual-purpose transport, vessel repairs, crew wages, bar-kept salvage charges, and legal fees—are cleared primarily via SWIFT MT103 for individual payments and MT202 COV for bank-to-bank transfers. For high-value project settlements, Luxembourg banks offer commercial letters of credit (L/C) and documentary collections; a standby L/C is commonly issued in favour of the salvage counter-party or port/terminal operator. Domestic Luxembourg clearings use the TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) and SEPA CT for euro operations. Simultaneous transfer facilities in USD are executed via the correspondent network of the Luxembourg bank (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, Société Générale, or Spuerkeess), and contract denominations under the Lloyds Standard Form of Salvage Agreement (LOF) are typically USD-denominated, requiring direct USD settlement with same-day value.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX options and option combinations (collars, strangles)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted convertible currencies, executed through CSSF-regulated credit institutions and cleared under EMIR where applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing with RCS (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (calendar-year filers: by 31 July); extension to 30 September available upon reasoned request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to EUR 25,000; persistent non-filing for two consecutive years may trigger judicial strike-off from the RCS and personal liability of the manager.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE) maintained by the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of the initial UBO declaration or of any material change filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines ranging from EUR 250 to EUR 125,000 per violation; repeated non-compliance can lead to administrative strike-off and manager liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Tax Return (Déclaration annuelle des sociétés de personnes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May following the tax year; automatic extension to 31 December for e-filers with professional representation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to EUR 20,000; monthly late-payment interest of 0.8% accrues on any partner-level tax assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total over EUR 20 million, net turnover over EUR 40 million, or average employees over 250; otherwise the partnership agreement may require a voluntary audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts); IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements or specialized fund vehicles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The manager must file an annual confirmation with the RBE that all natural-person beneficial owners remain accurate and current; any transfer of partnership interests or change in control requires a supplementary declaration within 30 days of the transaction.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,200 – 9,500 per annum if audit threshold triggered; otherwise none

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (main CIT rate for FY2025 as adopted by the Budget Law of December 2024; 15% applies to the first EUR 175,000 of taxable profit; plus 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT and municipal business tax of 6.75% in Luxembourg City, yielding an aggregate headline rate of approximately 24.94%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp default pass-through: 0% CIT at entity level; partners taxed on allocated shares at CIT or PIT level. Opaque election available under Article 174bis LIR. Participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income where the partner holds at least 10% or acquired the participation for at least EUR 1.2 million and satisfies the 12-month holding period. IP box regime: 80% exemption for qualifying IP income. Horizontal fiscal unity (Article 164bis LIR) available for 95%-owned Luxembourg subsidiaries.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit; annual set-off limited to 90% of taxable income pursuant to the Law of 14 December 2016; no 5-year cap applies)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 - Declaration for corporate income tax (impot sur le revenu des collectivites), municipal business tax (impot commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impot sur la fortune); mandatory electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu (Administration des contributions directes - ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the year following the close of the tax year for e-filing (e.g., FY2024 return due 31 December 2025); paper returns, where still permitted, due by 30 June of the following year; the ACD may grant extensions upon reasoned request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg tax identification number, RCS number, legal form, registered office, place of effective management, and identification of each general and limited partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be listed with foreign tax ID, jurisdiction of residence, hold percentage, and profit-share entitlement; TRC annex for each foreign partner where treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B - Financial Statements / Resultat comptable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and income statement of the SCSp covering the fiscal year, including towage and salvage contract revenue, freight/salvage remuneration, bunker costs, crew wages, and depreciation of tug vessels.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Financial statements must be prepared in EUR; foreign-currency contracts (e.g., Lloyd's Open Form URF remuneration) must be converted at the ECB reference rate; non-resident revenue must be attributed to the transparent partnership and allocated pro rata to partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part C - Tax adjustments / Resultat fiscal
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable result: add-back of non-deductible expenses, disallowed interest, 50% of certain director fees, and adjustments for related-party transfer pricing; deduction of tax-exempt shipping/salvage income and participation-exempt dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure that arm's-length towage and salvage fees charged to group vessels are supported by TP documentation; add-back of any excess non-arm's-length charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss offset (resultat fiscal), reduced by tax losses carried forward (maximum 90% offset), yielding the final forward tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the SCSp are allocated to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement; non-resident corporate partners may only use such losses to the extent permitted by their domestic loss-offset rules and applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 460 - Impot sur le revenu des collectivites (CIT)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of CIT at 15%/17%, plus 7% solidarity surcharge, after application of participation exemption and other deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp is transparent, no CIT is computed at Box 460 for non-resident partners; if the SCSp opted for opaque taxation, non-resident partners receive credit for Luxembourg CIT under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax base and tax at the communal multiplier (6.75% in Luxembourg City; variation by commune).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A transparent SCSp carrying on commercial activity in Luxembourg remains subject to ICC at entity level; non-resident partners do not benefit from full ICC credit unless the DTA so provides.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 500 - Partner allocation schedule / Annexe SCSp
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income, losses, tax credits, and withholding taxes to each partner in proportion to their capital-equalization and profit-share clauses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident LP partners, confirm that the SCSp has not created a Luxembourg permanent establishment; treaty protection (typically Article 5 and 7 OECD Model) must be documented; UBO declarations via the RCS register are mandatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge on the tax due (minimum EUR 250); late-payment interest at the statutory rate of 0.6% per month on outstanding principal; taxation d'office (ex officio assessment) with burden on the taxpayer; additional 5% surcharge for understatements and up to 100% surcharge for deliberate concealment, plus criminal prosecution for repeat or fraudulent non-filing.
